approach.label: Approach
approach.title: We don’t paint pretty pictures. We build
approach.body: A beautiful website with no job to do is just a postcard. So we start with the question “what should change in the business?” and only then choose the form, the stack and the flows.

principles.title: Problem first
principles.text: We ask about your clients, the flow of enquiries and the bottleneck. Design and technology follow — they’re never the starting point.

principles.title: Transparent
principles.text: A fixed quote, a demo every week, and you hold the access and source code from day one.

principles.title: Built to last
principles.text: We hand over the project with documentation and a month of edits. You’re never left alone with a black box.

approach.quote: A good digital tool never shouts about itself. It simply works — and you can see it in the enquiries.

cases.label: Work
cases.title: Selected
cases.intro: Live projects and concepts, put together to show how we think: interface, code and measurable value.
cases.note: Concepts were created to showcase design and are not commercial studio projects. Live projects can be opened via the link.

items.name: Yasna
items.summary: A cinematic photo story: seventeen photographs, ten chapters and a build with zero dependencies.
items.challenge: Tell a photo story as a single journey rather than a gallery with buttons — and keep it fast, readable and accessible on a phone.
items.solution: Photographs are pinned to the stage, chapters switch on scroll, and images load in stages: preview first, then full resolution. Without JavaScript the page remains readable.
items.result: Seventeen full-screen photographs, ten chapters, LQIP placeholders and staged loading. A live project.

items.name: Central Park
items.summary: A website for a park café in Vawkavysk: the atmosphere of the place, the menu and a short route to a visit.
items.challenge: A small café needed a clear shopfront online — one you’re not embarrassed to share on Instagram or put behind a QR code.
items.solution: A single-page site with a sense of place, a menu, a gallery and contact details. Lightweight static code with no unnecessary dependencies.
items.result: A live site that loads fast, works on a phone and needs no maintenance.

items.name: Spadchyna
items.summary: A shop for Belarusian ceramics: a catalogue, the makers’ stories and ordering through Telegram.
items.challenge: Present handmade goods as valuable objects rather than marketplace listings — and simplify ordering to two steps.
items.solution: A dark gallery-style storefront, large photographs, filters by maker and ordering via Telegram. The graphics are built on pixel embroidery.
items.result: Concept: a catalogue, product page, cart and an ordering flow in the messenger.

items.name: PraBot
items.summary: An AI administrator for a service studio: it answers questions about services, calculates a quote and books a call.
items.challenge: The studio was losing enquiries at night and at weekends, while the administrator burned hours on repetitive questions.
items.solution: A Telegram bot with a knowledge base, price calculation and hand-off of hot leads to a human. It books calls and reminds clients about meetings.
items.result: Concept: dialogue, quote calculation, booking and notifications in the admin chat.

items.question: What does a website for my business cost?
items.answer: It depends on scope: the number of pages, the design and the integrations. See the plans and the calculator for an indication. Write a couple of lines about the job — we’ll send an exact quote within a day, free and with no obligation.

items.question: Who writes the copy and chooses the photos?
items.answer: By default you supply the copy and we edit and assemble it. Copywriting and image selection can be handled by us — that’s a separate line in the quote.

items.question: What’s included in the month of edits?
items.answer: Copy and image changes, small refinements, bug fixes, help with publishing. New sections and redesigns are quoted separately.

items.question: What does “AI for business” actually mean?
items.answer: We set up workflows where a neural network takes on repetitive tasks: answering clients from your knowledge base, drafting replies and posts, sorting reviews. We don’t “do AI for the sake of AI”.

items.question: Do you work under contract? How does payment work?
items.answer: Yes, under contract. Standard terms are 30% up front and 70% after handover; larger projects are split into stages. Payment is in Belarusian roubles.

items.question: What if I don’t like the result?
items.answer: We demo every week and sign off the design before development, so the project never heads off “the wrong way”. If we realise at the start that we’re not aligned on the vision, we’ll say so honestly before any money changes hands.

items.question: What happens if you stop responding?
items.answer: All access, the domain, hosting and source code are in your name. The site runs independently of the studio, and full documentation is handed over at delivery.

items.question: How much of my time will this take?
items.answer: One conversation at the start (30–40 minutes) and a couple of short sign-offs. Everything else is our job.

items.question: Which languages can the site be in?
items.answer: Russian, Belarusian and English — with switching and a shared codebase. We can write the copy ourselves or translate yours.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.metaDescription: How Digital Belarus handles visitors’ data: no analytics cookies and no sharing with third parties.
privacy.intro: In short: we don’t set analytics cookies, we don’t sell data, and we use the information from the form only to reply to your enquiry.

sections.title: What data we collect
sections.body: Only what you enter in the form: name, contact details, a description of the job and your budget. The form doesn’t send data to a server: the enquiry text is composed in the browser, copied to the clipboard and opened in Telegram — you confirm the send.

sections.title: Why we collect it
sections.body: To reply to your enquiry, prepare a quote and discuss the project. We don’t use your data for marketing without separate consent.

sections.title: Cookies and analytics
sections.body: The site doesn’t use analytics or advertising cookies. Your chosen language is stored in the page address, not in a cookie.

sections.title: Sharing with third parties
sections.body: We don’t share data with third parties except where required by law. Conversations on Telegram are governed by Telegram’s own policy.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.body: You can ask us to delete the conversation and related data by messaging us on Telegram. We’ll delete it within a reasonable period.

sections.title: Contact
sections.body: For data protection questions, message us on Telegram: @kuzminklk.
